questions.question_text: The proportion of people aged above 65 years in the UK according to the figures from the 2001 census was approximately:
questions.explanation: The proportion of people aged over 65 was about 16% and is projected to increase to 23% by 2031.

questions.question_text: In the UK, among people above the age of 80 the proportion of people having dementia is:
questions.explanation: About 1 in 5 people aged above 80 in the UK have dementia and about 1 in 20 aged above 65 have dementia.

questions.question_text: All of the following are neuropsychological deficits seen in dementia, except:
questions.explanation: Alexithymia is not a cognitive symptom. It is defined as a person's inability to describe his or her own emotions and mood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common neuropsychiatric feature seen in dementia?
questions.explanation: Depression is the most common neuropsychiatric feature; some studies have quoted figures of up to 66% of patients having depressive features at some point during their illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following imaging techniques can be used to measure glucose metabolization in different parts of the brain?
questions.explanation: Functional imaging looks at brain function. A PET scan using the ligand fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) can be used to measure glucose utilization by different parts of the brain. A SPECT scan is generally used to measure the perfusion in different parts of the brain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neurotransmitter systems is mainly involved in the mechanism of action of galantamine?
questions.explanation: Galantamine is a reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase and it also has nicotinic receptor agonist properties.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the main neurotransmitter pathway through which memantine exerts its action?
questions.explanation: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist that affects glutamate transmission.

questions.question_text: What are 'Lewy bodies' (the pathological hallmark of dementia with Lewy bodies)?
questions.explanation: Lewy bodies are intracellular neuronal inclusion bodies that are made up of aggregated filaments of alpha-synuclein.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an instrument for assessment of cognitive functions?
questions.explanation: PANSS is the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale, which is used for schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding Pick's disease?

options.text: It is primarily a posterior brain pathology
It is characterized by loss of pyramidal neurons
It is characterized by enlarged lateral ventricles
Intracellular inclusion bodies are called Pick bodies

correct_answer.text: It is primarily a posterior brain pathology

correct_answers.text: It is primarily a posterior brain pathology

questions.explanation: The pathology is frontal and not posterior.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease?

options.text: It is most commonly seen in people above the age of 80
It is the most common form of Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease
Dementia is a common presenting feature
Histological brain changes are described as spongy in appearance
Neurological deficits are common, including ataxia

correct_answer.text: It is most commonly seen in people above the age of 80

correct_answers.text: It is most commonly seen in people above the age of 80

questions.explanation: Sporadic CJD is usually seen in the fifth and sixth decades.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a gene that has been linked with dementias?
questions.explanation: NMDA is a glutamate receptor and not a gene.

questions.question_text: 'Imitation' and 'utilization' behaviours have been described in which of the following syndromes?
questions.explanation: The orbitofrontal syndrome presents with changes in personality and social interaction characterized by egocentricity, disinhibition and occasionally imitation and utilization.

questions.question_text: In which of the following conditions is the 'fluid void sign' typically seen on imaging?
questions.explanation: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following imaging investigations would you avoid in a patient with a cardiac pacemaker while investigating for dementia?
questions.explanation: MR scanning should be avoided to prevent the strong magnetic field from interfering with cardiac pacemaker function.

questions.question_text: In an elderly patient on warfarin, which of the following antidepressants is most likely to interfere with its metabolism?
questions.explanation: The anticoagulant effect is enhanced; the pharmacokinetic interaction is through hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes.

questions.question_text: In an elderly patient, how long a wash-out period would you advise while switching from an SSRI such as citalopram to moclobamide?
questions.explanation: Moclobamide is an RIMA (reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase) and has an advantage over conventional MAOIs in that it does not need a wash-out period when switching from an SSRI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scenarios is likely to increase the risk of lithium toxicity in elderly patients?
questions.explanation: Most diuretics are likely to increase the excretion of sodium, which would make elderly people more prone to reduced lithium clearance and at greater risk of toxicity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a core feature of delirium?
questions.explanation: Catatonia is not considered a core clinical feature of delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following terms would best describe the behaviour of a patient with delirium who is aroused, restless, wandersome and pulling repeatedly at the clothing?
questions.explanation: Carphologia is described in delirium as picking, pulling and grabbing imaginary objects and the patient's own clothes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a predisposing factor for delirium?
questions.explanation: Male sex is a predisposing factor for delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following group of drugs is least likely to cause delirium?
questions.explanation: SSRIs act predominantly through the serotonin system, while others have action on the cholinergic system, GABA system, histamine receptors, etc., which are implicated in memory, sedation, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following strategies is least likely to help with the management of a patient with delirium on a medical ward?
questions.explanation: Movement restriction can aggravate delirium; physiotherapy is helpful.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best indicates the prevalence figures reported in literature for late-life depression
questions.explanation: A range of prevalence figures have been reported for late-life depression with an average figure of 13.5%. Major depression is less common (1–3%).

questions.question_text: What proportion of older people with dementia are expected to have depression?
questions.explanation: About a quarter of people with dementia develop depressive illness at some point during the course of their illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a contributing factor to risk of suicide in older people?
questions.explanation: Residential care is a protective factor for suicide in older people.

questions.question_text: The genetic risk of depression in older people is:

options.text: The same as in younger adults
Significantly higher than in younger adults

questions.explanation: The genetic risk is lower in later life. People with late-onset depression have fewer than half as many relatives with a history of depression as people with young-onset depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most important risk factor for late-onset depression?
questions.explanation: Cerebrovascular disease is one of the major risk factors for late-onset depression; the combination has recently been described as vascular depression.

questions.question_text: What percentage of people between the ages of 65 and 75 can be considered to be sexually active?
questions.explanation: 20% of people aged 65–75 are sexually active (having intercourse at least once a month).

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of beds is occupied by people above the age of 65 in a typical general hospital?
questions.explanation: 10–25% of people over the age of 65 admitted to medical wards are affected by delirium.

questions.question_text: What is the most common reason for liaison referrals in old age psychiatry?
questions.explanation: The two most common reasons for liaison old age psychiatry referrals are dementia and delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding general hospital personnel?

options.text: They are good at identifying psychiatric illnesses
They are poor at identifying psychiatric illnesses
There is no difference from psychiatric services

correct_answer.text: They are poor at identifying psychiatric illnesses

correct_answers.text: They are poor at identifying psychiatric illnesses

questions.explanation: A number of studies (see Philpot et al. 2005) have shown that general hospital personnel are poor at identifying psychiatric illnesses, especially depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true of medically ill patients with delirium?

options.text: They stay in hospital for a longer time
They are less likely to be institutionalized
They are more likely to have cognitive impairment
Complete resolution of delirium is less likely

correct_answer.text: They are less likely to be institutionalized

correct_answers.text: They are less likely to be institutionalized

questions.explanation: Medically ill people with delirium are more likely to be institutionalized on discharge from hospital.

questions.question_text: A combination of cognitive impairment and 'alien limb phenomenon' is seen in:
questions.explanation: Cortical basal degeneration usually presents in late middle or early old age, with akinesia, rigidity, limb apraxia, supranuclear gaze palsy, myoclonus, limb dystonia and cortical sensory loss.

questions.question_text: Which syndrome commonly presents with dementia, Parkinsonian symptoms and difficulty in downward gaze?
questions.explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy presents as an akinetic-rigid syndrome with subcortical dementia; it is also known as Steele–Richardson–Olszewski syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which illness presents with the classical clinical triad of dementia, myoclonic jerks and periodic EEG?
questions.explanation: Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease is a very rare form of rapidly progressing dementia; EEG is always abnormal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding Wilson's disease?

options.text: It is a disorder of copper metabolism
Low serum copper levels are a feature
Elevated urine copper levels are a feature

questions.explanation: Wilson's disease is transmitted as an autosomal-recessive trait.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms is the least common in late-onset schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Positive symptoms are more common (approximately 46% have at least one first rank symptom). Negative symptoms are the least common.

questions.question_text: Which of the following risk factors is the least important in late-onset schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: A positive family history is much less common among people with late-onset schizophrenia than among younger people with schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an important element of capacity?

options.text: Understanding the decision to be made

questions.explanation: A patient might refuse to see a doctor or another professional and yet retain the capacity to make a particular decision.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the assessment of capacity?

options.text: Capacity should be assumed unless proved otherwise
Capacity is specific to a decision
Capacity cannot change in an individual
Capacity can be influenced by communication problems
Undue influence has to be considered

correct_answer.text: Capacity cannot change in an individual

correct_answers.text: Capacity cannot change in an individual

questions.explanation: Capacity can vary considerably in an individual over a short space of time, especially in people who are medically ill.

questions.question_text: Elder abuse most commonly occurs in:
questions.explanation: The majority of elder abuse occurs in elderly people's own homes.

questions.question_text: The elements of sleep hygiene include all of the following, except:

options.text: Going to bed early in the evening
Using the bedroom only for sleep
Making the bed as comfortable as possible

correct_answer.text: Going to bed early in the evening

correct_answers.text: Going to bed early in the evening

questions.explanation: Going to bed early in the evening can lead to late-night sleep disturbance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following hypnotics could be most useful for early-morning wakefulness in older people?
questions.explanation: Oxazepam is considered to be more useful for early-morning wakefulness due to its intermediate half-life. Short-acting benzodiazepines such as lorazepam can be used for sleep-onset problems. Long-acting benzodiazepines such as diazepam and chlordiazepoxide are not recommended for use as hypnotics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not essential for the diagnosis of dementia?
questions.explanation: Perceptual abnormalities are not essential for the diagnosis of dementia.

questions.question_text: What percentage of all dementia cases is accounted for by Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: The most common dementia is Alzheimer's disease, followed by vascular dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a common symptom of frontotemporal dementia?
questions.explanation: Visual hallucinations are an unlikely feature of frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychological symptoms is most commonly seen in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Delusions are seen in about 30% of cases of Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common behavioural symptom of Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Apathy is the most common behavioural symptom and has been reported in up to 70% of cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following perceptual abnormalities is most common in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Visual hallucinations are the most common perceptual abnormalities in Alzheimer's disease. About 21% of patients report perceptual abnormalities, of whom 14% have visual hallucinations and about 7% have auditory hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to be effective in treating apathy in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: There is no licensed treatment for apathy in Alzheimer's disease but there is some evidence that cholinesterase inhibitors might be effective.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Female gender is one of the possible risk factors for Alzheimer's disease, although it is still not clear whether the higher rates of Alzheimer's disease in females are due to a relatively longer lifespan in women or result from a true risk factor.

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients have early-onset (below age 65) Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: About 5% of all Alzheimer's disease patients have an early onset and they are likely to have a stronger familial risk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a protective factor for Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: The apolipoprotein E2 allele is a possible protective factor, while the E4 allele is an established risk factor for Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: What is the median survival time for Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: A number of studies have shown that the median survival time for Alzheimer's disease (from diagnosis to death) is about 5–6 years.

questions.question_text: Abnormal aggregations of which of the following proteins are seen in Lewy bodies?
questions.explanation: Lewy bodies are primarily made up of aggregates of filamentous alpha-synuclein proteins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not considered a core feature of dementia with Lewy bodies?
questions.explanation: Repeated falls, although common in Lewy body dementia, are not considered a core feature.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding psychotic symptoms in Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: Use of cholinesterase inhibitors may be beneficial
Use of antipsychotics may be beneficial
Persistent contradiction of delusional ideas by caregivers may be helpful
They may lead to early institutionalization

correct_answer.text: Persistent contradiction of delusional ideas by caregivers may be helpful

correct_answers.text: Persistent contradiction of delusional ideas by caregivers may be helpful

questions.explanation: It is usually unhelpful for caregivers of people with Alzheimer's disease to contradict their delusional ideas.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms is not commonly seen in the early stage of frontotemporal dementia?

options.text: Lack of personal and social awareness

questions.explanation: Amnesia is rarely seen in the early stages of frontotemporal dementia, which commonly presents with slow onset of deterioration of personality, behaviour and speech.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common EEG finding in frontotemporal dementia?
questions.explanation: The EEG is normal in the vast majority of cases of frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotropic medications has the lowest risk of causing delirium?
questions.explanation: Citalopram and other SSRIs have the lowest risk of causing delirium.

questions.question_text: Among older people, the male:female suicide ratio in the UK is:
questions.explanation: Suicide rates increase in elderly people in comparison with the working population. In the UK, about 15% of the population is elderly, but around 25% of suicide occurs in the elderly.
